title: Supply Chain Dependency Resolution
business: A global electronics manufacturer managing complex multi-tier component dependencies.
problem: When a specific raw material becomes unavailable, the manufacturer struggles to identify the full downstream impact across nested sub-assemblies, leading to production bottlenecks.
solution: By modeling the bill of materials as a directed graph, Depth-First Search (DFS) allows the system to traverse deep into a specific component branch to map every affected sub-assembly before backtracking to evaluate other independent product lines.
steps: Represent the bill of materials as a directed graph where nodes are components and edges represent assembly dependencies.
Select the unavailable raw material node as the starting source for the traversal.
Utilize a DFS algorithm to explore the deepest branch of the dependency tree to identify all affected sub-assemblies.
Backtrack systematically to ensure no secondary assembly paths are overlooked.
Generate a comprehensive report of all impacted final products based on the traversal order.
outcome: The manufacturer gains a clear, granular view of production risks, allowing for proactive supply chain adjustments before a shortage halts assembly lines.
limitation: DFS can become inefficient in extremely deep or cyclic graphs, potentially leading to stack overflow errors; monitor the recursion depth or use iterative implementations to mitigate this risk.

questions.question: In Supply Chain Dependency Resolution, what is the primary benefit of using DFS?
options: It maps every affected sub-assembly by exploring deep branches before backtracking.
It identifies the most popular components in the warehouse.
It calculates the exact cost of raw materials.
It optimizes the physical layout of the factory floor.
questions.explanation: DFS is specifically suited for exploring deep dependency paths, which is necessary to identify all downstream impacts of a component shortage.

questions.question: What is a known limitation when applying DFS in Supply Chain Dependency Resolution?
options: It is too slow for small graphs.
It can cause stack overflow errors in very deep or cyclic graphs.
It requires a database connection for every node.
questions.explanation: Deep graphs can exceed the recursion limit of standard DFS implementations, necessitating monitoring or iterative approaches.
